Thanks for the ping — quick technical note: some calendar clients treat a DTSTART without an explicit TZID as a "floating" time (no timezone anchor). When a floating event crosses domains or gets forwarded, the receiving client will interpret it in the recipient's default zone which can flip AM/PM.

What I see in the .ics you attached: DTSTART:20270429T150000 (no TZID) and no VTIMEZONE block for Europe/London. That explains Andrew seeing 03:00.

Remediation options (fast):
- Recreate the invite with DTSTART in UTC (DTSTART:20270429T140000Z) and include VTIMEZONE blocks. Most clients will then show the same wall-clock time across domains.
- Alternatively send the invite as an explicit Google Calendar event (share by email address) rather than an .ics attachment — Google-to-Google preserves TZ.

I'll generate a fixed .ics now and attach. Also suggest adding the UTC time in the event description to reduce confusion.

I'll attach: demo-invite-fixed.ics
